questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the rear brake first.
Reduce speed and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Press the brakes firmly and stay calm if they lock.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What happens when motorcycles keep their headlights on during the day?

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
Other drivers see them better than when headlights are off.
Other drivers are often confused.
They are less safe than when headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers see them better than when headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers during the day.

questions.question: Which sign may be rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors make cars appear to be?

options.text: Larger
Farther away
Faster
Narrower

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Where should you ride if hazards are on your left?

options.text: In the left part of the lane
In the right part of the lane
In any part of the lane
On the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right part of the lane
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right part of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead?

options.text: In the center of the lane
In the left part of the lane
In the right part of the lane
In a weaving pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind a car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: How do you maintain control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn
Keep the motorcycle from leaning
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path
Come to a complete stop before turning

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: What happens when you carry a passenger or cargo?

options.text: Acceleration is faster, but stopping takes longer
Both acceleration and stopping take longer
Acceleration takes longer, but stopping is faster
Both acceleration and stopping are faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Both acceleration and stopping take longer
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are small
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do
They should only be used when other vehicles are nearby
They are more complicated than car signals

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals to tell others about your plans. Use them every time you turn or change lanes, even if no one is near.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, if traffic is heavy.
Yes, during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Yes, if the rider is comfortable doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot ride between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
When the sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and another driver may cut in front of you. Increase your following distance in these situations.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, hand signals help riders communicate. If the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as effective as the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when operated correctly.

questions.question: Where are motorcyclists most likely to have conflicts with other drivers?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Riders should be extra careful when entering and passing through intersections.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding next to another vehicle because the driver may not see you and could move into your lane. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection for a rider?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide the same protection.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Ride slower than normal.
Use a shorter following distance than when riding alone.
Ride faster than normal.
Brake later than you would when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than normal.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when changing lanes or entering traffic.

questions.question: When should you shift gears during a turn?

options.text: While you are in the turn.
Before you enter the turn.
While changing power in the turn.
While riding the brake through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you enter the turn.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before entering a turn, not during it.

questions.question: What should you do if you must cross a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed steady to improve traction.
Do not worry about the conditions.
Keep the motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.
questions.explanation: The best choice is to avoid slippery roads entirely. If you cannot avoid them, keep your motorcycle upright and ride as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Lane sharing is:

options.text: Usually not allowed.
Encouraged in heavy traffic.
Safe because motorcycles need less space than cars.
Allowed if you have had your license for more than three years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not allowed.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane to operate safely, just like cars. Lane sharing is usually not allowed. Position your motorcycle so other drivers do not try to share your lane.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle allows the rider to:

options.text: Touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Have the seat level with their waist.
Have the seat 10 inches above their waist.
Have the seat 10 inches below their waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Keep your focus on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but fail to notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Footwear should have low heels to avoid catching on foot pegs or rough surfaces. Leather gloves or gloves made from durable material protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.
